author: groundxero
title: The Enemy at Home
content:
The belief that Democrats will dismantle a system designed to serve the rapacious greed of the war machine and the ruling billionaire class is a mirage.




 




CHRIS HEDGES




Nov 12




 




Power does not rest in the Congress. It does not rest in the courts. It does not even rest in the imperial presidency. It rests in the hands of Wall Street financiers, Silicon Valley, private equity firms, the fossil fuel industry, the predatory health care and pharmaceutical giants, agribusinesses and, most of all, the war industry.




 




No mainstream politician, including Bernie Sanders, dares utter a word against our entrenched militarism. If you do, you end up like Ralph Nader, who was turned into a pariah by a compliant media and our corporate-indentured political parties. Nader spoke the truth. He paid for his honesty.




 




We are about to witness the 

largest increase

 in war spending in American history with a proposed $1.5 trillion budget. The average taxpayer already shells out over $4,000 a 

year

 

to the war industry as consumer and environmental agencies are 

dismantled

, health care and education are defunded and programs such as 

Medicaid

 

and 

food stamps

 (the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) are slashed.




 




The new Pentagon budget will 

hand

 $58.5 billion to artificial intelligence and military command-and-control centers and see the effective 

merging

 of the United States and Israeli military industrial complexes. Seventy-four percent of the increase in the proposed $1.5 trillion budget 

will go to

 private contractors, 

including

 those who are building massive data centers on military bases.




 




None of this is good for us or good for the planet. The Pentagon, powered by the fossil fuel industry, is the world’s 

largest institutional polluter

, emitting an estimated 

66 million metric tons

 

of carbon dioxide in 2024.




 




Americans, meanwhile, struggle with rising prices — nearly 30 percent of people go 

into debt

 to buy groceries. An estimated 114,174. Americans 

die

 each year due to lack of health insurance or inadequate health care while a single-payer universal health care system could cover every American, save more than 100,000 lives a year, and reduce annual health expenditures by $1.04 trillion, or nearly 20 percent. Twenty-five percent of Americans are 

functionally unemployed

. The minimum wage remains frozen, despite Democratic Party promises to raise it, at $ 7.25 an hour.




 




The elites use war not only for personal enrichment, but to stifle class conflict.




 




War, as W.E.B. Du Bois said, diverts the poor from their real interests. It funnels national frustrations into the “heroic” battle against a common enemy. The nationalist cant, with its endemic racism, seduces those who are alienated or on the margins of society into feeling they suddenly belong. It entices them to sacrifice themselves for a “noble” cause. They becime the architects of their own enslavement. They march like sheep into war’s purgatory.




 




By the time they wake up, it is too late. They are cast aside, as so many of our 

veterans

 have painfully discovered, like human refuse.




 




But as a tactic to consolidate power and enrich the billionaire class, it is unbeatable.




 




Wars will only be curtailed, if not halted, when we nationalize the weapons industry and dramatically reduce the military budget. Until then, nothing, absolutely nothing, will change.




 




Indeed, things will only get worse.




 




No one in Congress — or any other branch of government — will do this for us.




 




The masters of war sitting in the boardrooms of Boeing, General Dynamics or Northrop Grumman are not praying for peace in the Middle East or coexistence with China and Russia. The generals — who build their careers by orchestrating wars and post military careers enriching themselves working for defense contractors — are not seeking a cessation of global conflicts. They are seeking hundreds of billions in taxpayer dollars and government debt to fuel the self-defeating cycle of endless war.




 




The corporate vultures — especially the war makers — are, as I write, descending on Congress. They are meeting with Democratic Party leaders and holding out promises of millions in cash. They will corrupt, neutralize and compromise most. They will destroy the careers of the very few who refuse to do their bidding.




 




They hold the real power. They have no intention of surrendering it.




 




The manufacturing of weapons systems and the waging of war are the chief activities of the U.S. government. It is no longer one among other means of advancing the national interest. War and violence are how we speak to the rest of the world.




 




The “shadow world,” — as the author Andrew Feinstein calls it in his 

book

 on the global arms trade — is defined by staggering levels of corruption, deception and senseless death. It is lawless and unregulated. Its criminal activities, cannibalization of national budgets and secrecy are sanctified in the name of “national security.”




 




Lockheed Martin, RTX (formerly Raytheon Technologies), Boeing, General Dynamics, Northrop Grumman, BAE Systems, Leonardo, Airbus, Rheinmetall and ThyssenKrupp, along with Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Palantir, Goldman Sachs, Citibank and Exxon, 

are

 the state.




 




We, including our political class, 

are

 the vassals.




 




The voters can send whoever they want to Congress, but until these corporations and the billionaire class are regulated, taxed and controlled, until their vast monopolies are broken up, until we stop squandering half of all discretionary spending on war, nothing will change.




 




Nothing.




 




Civilizations, as the historian Arnold J. Toynbee argued, “die from suicide, not by murder.” They are disemboweled by an uncontrollable and unaccountable military that drains state budgets and plunges dying empires into one military debacle after the next. These decaying civilizations finally collapse from within.




 




This is where we are headed.




 




The corporations, and the billionaires who run them, buy and trade politicians, academics and journalists like Pokémon cards. Their lobbyists write the legislation. They own the media. They have stifled the academy, shutting down free speech and purging critics. Judges offer them unlimited power. To defy them — and I speak from personal experience — is to be cast into the wilderness.




 




The military-industrial complex, as Karl Liebknecht said of German imperialists on the eve of World War I, is the enemy within.




 




“

Making a Killing: How the West Profits from Slaughter in Gaza and Yemen

,” co-authored by Andrew Feinstein, Ruth Rohde and Jack Cinamon — with contributions from Paul Holden and Professor Anna Stavrianakis — examines the global arms trade in the Middle East.




 




The authors estimate that $130 billion was made from arms exports by Western nations to Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates during the war on Yemen and over $50 billion from Israeli foreign military procurements.




 




“RTX Chairman and CEO Christopher T. Calio made $18 million in 2024, after being appointed halfway through the year, while his compensation package surged to almost $25 million in 2025,” the authors note. “His predecessor, Gregory Hayes, was remunerated to the tune of nearly $22 million in 2023. Lockheed Martin CEO and former U.S. Air Force pilot Jim Taiclet, who was deployed in Saudi Arabia while serving during the Gulf War, earns an annual package of more than $23 million. Since his appointment in 2020 he has raked in more than $136 million in total Lockheed Martin compensation.”




 




Phebe Novakovic, the CEO of General Dynamics, has a net worth estimated at $420 million, up $270 million since 2020.




 




But it is not only the CEOs who profit.




 




Members of Congress and their families 

traded

 between $24 million and $113 million worth of Pentagon contractor stocks in 2024.




 




Representative Josh Gottheimer from New Jersey — a Democrat — is a former Clinton speechwriter and a close ally of House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries. Gottheimer, who is 

heavily funded

 by the pro-Israel lobby and an ardent Zionist, 

traded

 $22 million worth of stock in the top 100 Pentagon contractors, including Microsoft — which received $414 million from the Department of Defense in 2023 for software and cloud computing services — Northrop Grumman and IBM.




 




Gottheimer serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Financial Services Committee. He is well placed to know which defense companies are enriched by government contracts and which are not.




 




Former Democratic House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, is not any better. She made an estimated $38.6 million profit in one year from her stock trading, the most of any lawmaker, in 2024.




 




These politicians run the Democratic Party. They carry out the same illegal insider trading and have the same conflicts of interest as the Republicans and the Trump White House. Hunter Biden is no less odious than Donald Trump Jr. and 

Eric Trump

.




 




“Honeywell — which provides sensors and guiding devices to assist the Israeli military in airstrikes in Gaza — is the most commonly held arms company stock among members of Congress, followed by RTX, the company that makes missiles for Israel’s Iron Dome, among other weapons systems,” the authors write.




 




Members of Congress, they report, “made more than 13,300 trades totaling over $635 million in 2025.”




 




The arms trade, the authors illustrate, has created an unelected, shadowy cabal of foreign policy, corporate and military officials, along with academics, who — no matter who is in the White House or the Congress — feed the military beast.




 




This cabal, many parked in think tanks funded by the defense industry and given prominent platforms on cable news channels, preach endless war. They ensure the fabrication of bombs, missiles, warplanes, drones, ships, tanks and guns. They ship these weapons around the globe. They sustain the interconnected network of cutting-edge, high-tech systems of information warfare and surveillance, powered by data processing centers, cloud technologies and artificial intelligence.




 




Once these weapons and tools of surveillance are tested on Palestinians or Yemenis, they are brought back to manage and surveil 

us —

 an imperial boomerang abolishing what is left of our civil liberties and freedom.




 




The tyranny empire imposes on others, as Thucydides reminded us, it finally imposes on itself.




 




The choice, as Rosa Luxemburg pointed out, is socialism or barbarism. If we do not dismantle global capitalism, if we do not free ourselves from the tentacles of the war industry, we will descend into the Hobbesian world of totalitarian capitalism, failed states, mass migrations, endless war, ecocide and permanent immiseration.




 




The 

genocide

 in Gaza is the harbinger of this coming dystopia. It is a stark message by the industrialized nations to the Global South, especially with the breakdown of the climate. The message is this:




 




There are no rules. International Humanitarian Law is dead. The strong will annihilate the weak. We control the world’s resources and most of its wealth. We will not relinquish it. Your suffering and lives are meaningless to us. Defy us and you too will be slaughtered.




 




Fear is the only language these vampires understand. This is a dark fact about human nature. It is why Richard Nixon was our last liberal president. Nixon was not a liberal. He was devoid of empathy. He lacked a conscience. But he was scared of movements. He knew the power of the strike.




 




It is not our job to take power. It is our job to create radical movements to hold power in check. Without these movements, we are doomed.




 




“You get freedom by letting your enemy know that you’ll do anything to get your freedom; then you’ll get it,” Malcolm X 

told

 young civil rights activists from Mississippi 51 days before his assassination on February 21, 1965. “When you get that kind of attitude, they’ll label you as a ‘crazy Negro,’ or they’ll call you a ‘crazy nigger’ — they don’t say Negro. Or they’ll call you an extremist or a subversive, or seditious, or a red, or a radical. But when you stay radical long enough, and get enough people to be like you, you’ll get your freedom…So don’t you run around here trying to make friends with somebody who’s depriving you of your rights. They’re not your friends, no, they’re your enemies. Treat them like that and fight them, and you’ll get your freedom; and after you get your freedom, your enemy will respect you. And I say that with no hate. I don’t have hate in me. I have no hate at all. I don’t have any hate. I’ve got some sense. I’m not going to let anybody who hates me tell me to love him.”




 




The disease of permanent war and militarism is devouring the guts of our nation. These forces snuff out democracy. They turn culture into nationalist cant and sentimental kitsch. They turn education and the media into echo chambers for the rich and the powerful. They wreck the economy. They immiserate the citizenry. They pump toxins into the air, soil and water. They strip us of our liberty. They foster moral nihilism.




 




War is the apotheosis of this corporate rule, designed to exploit people and the natural world until exhaustion or collapse.




 




And time is running out.




 




If we don’t transform this system we, and most other species, will go extinct.




 




Literally.




 




We must mobilize to defeat these forces. This means organized mass disruptions of government and commerce as we have seen in France, Spain and India, and with organizations such as 

Palestine Action

 and 

Just Stop Oil

.




 




If we remain supplicants, if we hope desperately for a feckless political class to save us, the barbarians will triumph.

by

Chris Hedges

 is a Pulitzer Prize–winning author and journalist who was a foreign correspondent for 15 years for The New York Times.

title: 544 Scientists and Researchers Stand with Siang Valley Anti-Dam Movement; Demand Halt to Mega Project and Release of Detained Activists
content:
“We stand with the people of the Siang Valley in their struggle to protect their river, their lands, their rights and the ability to determine their future. We recognise that the people who call this valley home must have the primary say in determining its future.”




 




Groundxero

 Desk




 




In a strong show of solidarity with the indigenous Adi communities resisting the proposed 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh, a group of 544 scientists, researchers, and concerned citizens working in the fields of nature, wildlife, society and the environment has called on the Union and state governments to immediately halt all pre-feasibility activities, withdraw additional security forces from the valley and release anti-dam protesters detained and arrested under the stringent Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA).




 




The statement, issued on November 9, 2026, comes amid growing resistance in the Siang Valley to the proposed mega-dam and reports of intensified security deployment, restrictions on people’s movement, arrests and the use of force against protesters.




 




The signatories, many of whom have worked in Arunachal Pradesh and the Eastern Himalayas, describe the Siang Valley as an ecologically irreplaceable landscape of immense biodiversity, cultural significance and traditional knowledge. Referring to an earlier statement by 114 scientists issued on June 9, 2025, they point out that 48 new species and 140 new distribution records have been documented in the valley in the past 15 years alone.




 




The statement warns that large-scale construction in an ecologically fragile and highly seismically active river system could have irreversible consequences. It emphasises that the Siang River, its forests and surrounding mountains sustain not only rich biodiversity but also the livelihoods, cultural identity and traditional knowledge systems of indigenous Adi communities.




 




The scientists express particular concern over the Arunachal Pradesh government’s continued efforts to push ahead with the project’s Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) despite sustained opposition from affected communities. They condemned the militarisation of this otherwise peaceful region, restrictions on movement, arrests and detentions of local anti-dam activists, and the use of tear gas and force against protesters. They also denounce the alleged harassment and intimidation of lawyers, journalists and others standing in solidarity of the movement.




 




Invoking the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), the signatories assert that the project must not proceed without the free, prior and informed consent of the affected indigenous communities, whose lands, livelihoods, cultural heritage and relationship with the Siang are at stake. They also stressed on the constitutional guarantees of freedom of speech, expression and peaceful assembly.




 




The statement calls on the Arunachal Pradesh and Union governments to stop all PFR-related activities, withdraw additional armed forces from the region, release those detained for participating in the movement, and initiate an open and meaningful dialogue with the affected communities.




 




The signatories affirm that the people who have protected and sustained the Siang Valley for generations must have the primary say in determining its future.




 




The full statement along with the list of signatories is published below:




 




November 9, 2026




 




We, a group of scientists, researchers, conservation practitioners and concerned citizens, many of whom have worked in Arunachal Pradesh and in the Eastern Himalaya, stand in unequivocal solidarity with the people of the Siang Valley in their opposition to the proposed 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP).




 




The Siang Valley is not merely a site for a proposed mega-infrastructure project. The Siang River, its forests and the surrounding mountains sustain extraordinary biodiversity, livelihoods, traditional knowledge systems and the cultural identity of indigenous Adi communities.




 




A statement issued by a collective of 114 scientists on 9th of June 2025, noted that the Siang is a rich living landscape of immense ecological, cultural and biological significance. In the past 15 years alone, there have been 48 new species described, as well as 140 new distribution records from the valley.




 




As scientists, researchers and citizens working in the fields of nature, wildlife, society and the environment, we recognise that the Siang Valley is an ecologically irreplaceable landscape, and much of its biodiversity and ecological complexity remains poorly understood.




 




The irreversible consequences of largescale interventions in such a fragile, extremely seismically active and biodiverse river system demand the utmost caution.




 




The people of the Siang valley have nurtured and protected these landscapes and species for generations. Their knowledge, lived experiences and concerns must be central to any decisions about their future.




 




We are deeply concerned by the Arunachal Pradesh government’s continued push to undertake the Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) for SUMP despite sustained opposition from affected communities. We are particularly saddened and alarmed by the deployment of large numbers of armed security personnel, restrictions on people’s movement, the arrest and detention of community members, and the use of tear gas and force against citizens.




 




The growing militarisation of this otherwise peaceful region is deeply disturbing and unacceptable. In a democratic country, communities have every right to question, oppose and refuse projects that they believe threaten their lands, cultures, livelihoods and futures. In keeping with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), the project must not proceed without the free, prior and informed consent (FPIC) of the affected indigenous communities, whose lands, livelihoods, cultural heritage and relationship with the Siang are at stake.




 




We also strongly condemn the harassment and intimidation of those supporting and documenting the events and the movement, including lawyers and journalists. Article 19 of the Constitution of India guarantees six fundamental freedoms, including the freedom of speech, expression and to assemble peacefully; the restrictions imposed by the state cannot be deemed as reasonable.




 




We therefore urge the Arunachal Pradesh and Union Governments to halt all PFR-related activities, withdraw the additional armed forces deployed in the region, release those detained for their participation in the movement, and engage in an open, transparent and meaningful dialogue with the affected communities, respecting their rights, agency and decisions.




 




Beyond ecological arguments, our work has taught us that protecting nature cannot be separated from respecting the people who have lived with, cared for and sustained these landscapes over generations.




 




We stand with the people of the Siang Valley in their struggle to protect their river, their lands, their rights and the ability to determine their future. We recognise that the people who call this valley home must have the primary say in determining its future.

title: দুনিয়া কাঁপানো শরৎকাল
content:
এরকম এক শরৎকাল প্রত্যক্ষ করার পর এক রকমের আশা জাগে – বসন্ত আসতে হয়তো বেশি দেরী হবে না।




 




দেবারতি

 

গুপ্ত

  




 




এ এক অন্য শরৎকাল এসে হাজির হয়েছে দুনিয়া জুড়ে। লেট ক্যাপিটালিজমের নখ দাঁত যেভাবে প্রকট হয়ে উঠেছে গত দুই দশকে তাতে সাধারণ মানুষের নাভিশ্বাস উঠতে শুরু করেছে। মিলেনিয়াল প্রজন্ম এই পরিস্থিতি একভাবে মোকাবিলা করেছে। তাদের যৌবনে তবু কিছু চাকরি ছিল মন ভোলানোর উপাদান ছিল। কোভিড পরবর্তী কালে যে প্রজন্ম যৌবনে পা দিয়েছে তারা পেয়েছে এক অবাক পৃথিবী। একদিকে সমাজ মাধ্যমের বিভ্রান্তিকর দুনিয়া আরেকদিকে নতুন হাজির হওয়া কৃত্রিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা। এইসবের মধ্যে দুনিয়াজোরা সরকারি শিক্ষা ব্যবস্থা, স্বাস্থ্য পরিষেবা আর কর্মসংস্থানের চূড়ান্ত বেহাল অবস্থা।




 




বছর দুই আগে থেকেই সার্বিয়ার ছাত্ররা বিক্ষোভ শুরু করেছিল। নোভি সাদ রেইল স্টেশনের ছাত ভেঙে ১৬ জনের মৃত্যু হওয়ায় ছাত্রদের বিরোধিতা শুরু হয়। ওই কান্ড নিছক দুর্ঘটনা বলে চাপা দেবার চক্রান্ত সহজে মেনে নেয় নি সার্বিয়ার ছাত্ররা। তারা আন্দোলন শুরু করে। সেই আন্দোলন দীর্ঘ ১৪ বছর ধরে ক্ষমতায় থাকা আলেক্সান্ডার ভুচিচকে সম্প্রতি গদিচ্যুত করেছে।




 




২৬ অক্টোবর, অর্থাৎ সার্বিয়ার ওই ঐতিহাসিক দিনে বেলগ্রেড থেকে এক সফটওয়্যার ইঞ্জিনিয়ার লাজার পেত্রোভিচ ‘কফি হাউস এক্সপেরিয়েন্স’ এর লাইভ পডকাস্টে এসেছিলেন। এই মুহূর্তে কলকাতা শহরে যেখানে প্রতিদিন ফ্যাসিজমের উপস্থিতি হাড়ে হাড়ে টের পাচ্ছি সেইখানে বসে সার্বিয়ার পার্লামেন্টের সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে উচ্ছ্বসিত লাজারকে দেখতে পাওয়া, নিঃসন্দেহে খুব আশাব্যঞ্জক ঘটনা। মজার কথা হল দক্ষিণপন্থী ভুচিচের এস এন এস (সার

title: Amid Ongoing Siang Protests, In-Principle Forest Clearance Nod to Naying Hydroelectric Project; Over One Lakh Trees to Be Felled
content:
The recommendation for in-principle forest clearance for the 1,000-MW Naying Hydroelectric Project in Arunachal Pradesh comes amid escalating protests against large dam projects in the Siang river basin. 

With 470.8 hectares of forest land set to be diverted, compensatory afforestation proposed 1,700 kilometres away in Madhya Pradesh, and landowners rejecting NEEPCO’s compensation offer, the 

Naying 

project on the Siyom River raises serious questions about ecological destruction, and the social cost of hydropower expansion 

in a region where indigenous communities are increasingly resisting such projects that threaten their forests, rivers and ancestral lands.




 




Groundxero

 

Desk




 




Amid growing opposition and resistance to the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh, another major hydroelectric project in the Siang river basin has moved closer to implementation. On October 23, 2026, the Forest Advisory Committee (FAC) of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 

recommended in-principle forest clearance

 for the 1,000-MW Naying Hydroelectric Project on the Siyom River (Yomgo River), a major tributary of the Siang.

content:
মোদি জমানার অর্থনৈতিক মডেলে ক্রোনি ক্যাপিটালিজম এক গুরুত্বপূর্ণ উপাদান। আইডিবিআই বিক্রি আরেকবার সেই সারসত্যকে প্রমাণ করল।




 




সুমন কল্যাণ মৌলিক




 




দেশের সম্পদ আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্ককে বিদেশি কোম্পানি ফেয়ারফ্যাক্সের হাতে তুলে দেওয়ার সরকারি সিদ্ধান্তের পেছনে লুকিয়ে থাকা অসাড় যুক্তি ও দেশ লুঠের এই ধারাবাহিক ইতিহাসের কথা ইতিমধ্যে বহুল আলোচিত (বর্তমান নিবন্ধকারের আইডিবিআই বিক্রির সরল রেসিপি শীর্ষক 

লেখাটি

 আগ্রহীরা পড়ে দেখতে পারেন)। কিন্তু বিষয়টি আর নীতি ও পদ্ধতির প্রশ্নে সীমাবদ্ধ নয়। এই চুক্তির অস্বচ্ছতা, ফেয়ারফ্যাক্সের লাভ, আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্কের সম্পদের অবমূল্যায়ণ সংক্রান্ত তথ্য ইতিমধ্যে বিজনেস ওয়ার্ল্ড ও হিন্দু বিজনেস লাইনের প্রশংসনীয় অন্তর্তদন্ত মূলক প্রতিবেদনের কারণে জনসমক্ষে চলে এসেছে। লোকসভায় বিরোধী দলনেতার সোসাল মিডিয়ায় টুইট, প্রাক্তন অর্থসচিব ও সমাজকর্মী ই এ এস শর্মার খোলা চিঠি ও আইডিবিআই ব্যাঙ্ক কর্মীদের অনশন-আন্দোলন বিতর্ককে নতুন মাত্রা দিয়েছে। মোদি জমানার বহু আর্থিক অস্বচ্ছতা মত এই চুক্তিতে ক্রোনি ক্যাপওটালিজমের ছায়া দীর্ঘতর হচ্ছে। সরকারি সম্পদকে বেসরকারি হাতে তুলে দেওয়ার ইতিহাসে বার বার দেখা যায় সম্পদের অবমূল্যায়ণ, স্বার্থের সংঘাতের অভিযোগ। ফেয়ারফ্যাক্সের আইডিবিআই কেনার ক্ষেত্রেও গল্পটা আলাদা কিছু হচ্ছে না।




 




আলোচনার সুবিধার্থে আমরা এই অসঙ্গতিগুলিকে পর পর আলোচনা করব। আইডিবিআইকে বিক্রির বিষয়ে ব্যাঙ্কের সম্পদের প্রাথমিক মূল্যায়ণের দায়িত্বে ছিল সরকারি সংস্থা ‘ডিপার্টমেন্ট অফ ইনভেস্টমেন্ট অ্যান্ড পাবলিক অ্যাসেট ম্যানেজমেন্ট (ডাইপাম)। এদের দায়িত্ব ছিল সমস্ত দিক

content:
ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে একের পর এক ঘটে চলা সংখ্যালঘু খ্রিষ্টান গীর্জার উপর হামলা, SIR প্রক্রিয়ায় ভোটারদের নাম বাদ দেওয়া, রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প তৈরি ও বেআইনি ভাবে সাধারণ মানুষদের সেখানে আটক করার বিরূদ্ধে ৩ নভেম্বর, মঙ্গলবার কলকাতার প্রেস ক্লাবে এক সংবাদিক সম্মেলন ডাকা হয়ে।

কলকাতা, ৩ নভেম্বর ২০২৬




 




নতুন সরকার পশ্চিমবঙ্গে ক্ষমতায় আসার পর কেটেছে মাত্র পাঁচ মাস। ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে ৪৮টি খ্রিষ্টান উপাসনালয়ে হামলা চালিয়েছে হিন্দুত্ববাদী দুষ্কৃতিরা। কিন্তু এফআইআর হয়েছে মাত্র ১৫ টি। এমনকি বহু জায়গায় পুলিশ এফ.আই.আর নিচ্ছে না। ‘কারওয়ানে মহব্বত’, ‘সবর ইনস্টিটিউট’ ও ‘আমরা এক সচেতন প্রয়াস’ নামক সংগঠনগুলির মিলিত তথ্যান্যসন্ধানে উঠে এসেছে এমনই বাস্তবচিত্র।




 




ভোট পরবর্তী সময়ে এ রাজ্যে একের পর এক ঘটে চলা সংখ্যালঘু খ্রিষ্টান গীর্জার উপর হামলা, SIR প্রক্রিয়ায় ভোটারদের নাম বাদ দেওয়া, রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে ডিটেনশন ক্যাম্প তৈরি ও বেআইনি ভাবে সাধারণ মানুষদের সেখানে আটক করার বিরূদ্ধে ৩ নভেম্বর, মঙ্গলবার কলকাতার প্রেস ক্লাবে এক সংবাদিক সম্মেলনের ডাক দেয় এই সংগঠনগুলি। সংবাদিক সম্মেলনে বক্তা হিসেবে উপস্থিত ছিলেন প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার জহর সরকার, প্রাক্তন আইএএস অফিসার ও সমাজকর্মী হর্ষ মন্দার, প্রাক্তন আইএএস ওয়াজাহাত হাবিবুল্লাহ, সংবাদিক আকার প্যাটেল, মানবাধিকার জন দয়াল এবং মানবাধিকার কর্মী বিদ্যা ডিঙ্কার।

title: Donald Trump’s Republicans suffer landslide defeat – what this means for the world
content:
The world should prepare itself for the possibility that a politically wounded and angry Trump could now decide to vent his frustrations abroad.




 




Andrew Gawthorpe

, 

Leiden University




 







Donald Trump’s Republican Party has received a stunning rebuke in the US midterm elections. Republicans went into the evening hoping that the polls might be wrong and that they could at least cling on to control of the Senate. But by midnight in Washington, the GOP was staring down what looked like its worst defeat in 50 years.




 




Republican losses were not just confined to the type of swing districts that parties usually worry about on 

election night

. The scale of the losses was staggering. They lost Senate seats in deep red states such as Texas and South Carolina. They lost districts they had 

gerrymandered

 and in which they were supposed to be unbeatable. They lost seats that even the sharpest analysts thought were safe.




 




Why? For months, 

surveys have shown

 that voters are fed up with high prices, with the war in Iran, and with what is increasingly being talked about as the Trump administration’s corruption. author: groundxero
title: Where Women Make History: Reclaiming Agency in History and in Movements
content:
Gargi’s book is a historiographical recovery of the junctures when women fought and moved another inch towards occupying half the sky. 




 




By

 Vertika Mani 




 




The first intriguing thing to notice about V. Gargi’s 

No Women, No History

 is the cover page of the book itself. Published by Virasam Books, the cover depicts women holding guns, marching with axes and also hugging trees. The image with its wide range of contrast yet a commonality of women as marchers and fighters interacts with its readers to convey the larger argument that this book seeks to make. The book was initially written as a collection of notes by V. Gargi, a revolutionary activist who dedicated this book 

“To all the women who fought against overwhelming odds, made great sacrifices to the extent of even laying down their lives to make this place better for all of us…”







 




The first edition of 

No Women No History: Women in Indian Movements (19th century – 2004)

 was published last year in August, at a pit stop, when the mainstream feminist discourse in India and abroad mostly associate women with power of intellect and pen, which are all quite a matter of privilege and can therefore be politically disabling at times. In that context, reading 

No women No History

 is refreshing as it takes us down the road of history of women’s struggle, almost on a rampage to discover the truth

title: Villagers Barred from Public Hearing on Rs 10,000-Crore Steel Project in Raghunathpur, Purulia; Allege Police Repression
content:
Accusing the administration of staging a secretive, stage-managed public hearing for Shakambhari Ispat and Power Ltd in Purulia, villagers blocked a state highway, raising concerns over air pollution, water scarcity, and loss of farmland and the health of communities already living amid polluting industries.




 




Raghunathpur, October 28, 2026: 

Residents of several villages in Raghunathpur sub-division of West Bengal’s Purulia district blocked the Raghunathpur–Santaldihi State Highway on Wednesday in protest against the public hearing for a proposed Rs 10,000-crore steel and power complex of Shakambhari Ispat and Power Ltd. The villagers accuse the administration of keeping them out of the hearing, held at the office of the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) of Raghunathpur, by deploying a large police force, barricading the approach and locking the main gate, while a handful of people allegedly handpicked by the company were allowed inside, so that what they describe as a farcical hearing could be staged to manufacture public consent for the project.




A large police force, barricaded the approach and locked the main gate of the SDO office
